title: Random Neural Network Expressivity for Non-Linear Partial Differential Equations
claim: Approximation error decays with network width at roughly the predicted square-root rate, even in dimensions beyond the theory's scope.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, left-to-right, dashed theoretical-rate curve overlaid on empirical curve
description: Two line plots sit side by side. Panel (a) is for d=4 and panel (b) is for d=5. In each, the x-axis is network width N, from 0 to about 7500. The y-axis is relative L2 error, from 0 to 1. A solid blue line with dot markers shows the RaNN error, with a light-blue shaded band for one standard deviation. A dashed dark-gray curve shows the theoretical C/sqrt(N) rate. A legend sits in the top right of each panel. The error drops steeply at small widths, then flattens into a long tail. In (a) the empirical curve almost coincides with the dashed rate. In (b) it stays above the dashed curve at mid widths and approaches it at large widths. The grid is light and the palette is blue and gray. The eye goes first to the steep drop at the left of each curve.
caption: Approximation error of RaNNs solving PME in dimensions d = 4, 5 with varying widths. The shaded band indicates the region within one standard deviation of the mean relative L2 error.
abstract: Neural networks with randomly generated hidden weights (RaNNs) have been extensively studied, both as a standalone learning method and as an initialization for fully trainable deep learning methods. In this work, we study RaNN expressivity for learning solutions to non-linear partial differential equations (PDEs). Despite their widespread use in practical applications, a rigorous theoretical understanding of the approximation properties of RaNNs in this context remains limited. Here, we derive error bounds for RaNN approximations to time-dependent Sobolev functions and obtain a dimension-free approximation rate $\frac{1}{2}$ for sufficiently regular functions. We apply our results to two important classes of non-linear PDEs: Porous Medium Equations and Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations, showing that RaNNs are capable of efficiently approximating solutions to these complex, non-linear PDEs. Our theoretical analysis is supported by numerical experiments, showing that the obtained convergence rates extend beyond the considered setting.
